sets.title: Monsoon Forecasts and Farmers
sets.text: For decades, Indian farmers read the sky the way their grandparents did: by watching the first cloudbank over the Western Ghats and trusting the village almanac. Today the India Meteorological Department issues forecasts based on satellite images, ocean temperature records and supercomputer models, and its seasonal outlook in April is watched closely by markets as well as farmers. Accuracy has improved, yet a district-level prediction remains hard, because rainfall in a single week can differ sharply between two villages only ten kilometres apart. Critics argue that a headline figure such as 'ninety-six per cent of the long period average' tells a smallholder very little about when to sow. Officials reply that the national figure was never meant to replace local advice, and they point to text-message alerts that now reach millions of farmers in their own languages. Whether these alerts are changing decisions in the field is still being studied; early surveys suggest that farmers trust a forecast more when it comes through a neighbour than through a phone.

sets.title: Threads of a Fading Craft
sets.text: In a weaver's colony near Pochampally, the clatter of the loom starts before sunrise and often continues after dark. A single sari in the traditional ikat style may take a family several days, since the threads must be tied and dyed in patterns before weaving even begins. Power looms can imitate the design in a few hours and sell it at half the price, and many shoppers cannot tell the difference at first glance. The government has tried to help by reserving certain designs for handloom producers and by organising exhibitions in big cities. These steps have helped some weavers, but a young man in the colony shrugged when asked if he would follow his father's trade. His cousin, he said, earns more as a delivery rider. The cloth, it seems, may survive better than the craft that produces it.

questions.questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that farmers
options: may act on a forecast more readily when someone they know passes it on
have stopped using any kind of weather prediction
no longer need information at the district level
are unaffected by satellite-based forecasting in any way
questions.explanation: The last sentence reports that farmers trust a forecast more when it comes through a neighbour. The other options either contradict the passage (they still need local advice) or go beyond it.

questions.questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that before the franchise league
options: most kabaddi players earned little money from the sport
kabaddi was unknown in all Indian villages
girls were not allowed to watch kabaddi
there were no referees in kabaddi matches
questions.explanation: The passage says players once earned only the praise of their villages, which implies little or no money. The other options are not supported.

questions.questionText: The passage suggests that if millets fetched unsteady prices, many farmers would
options: keep growing the more profitable crops they already know
switch completely to millets for health reasons
stop farming altogether
insist that schools stop buying millets
questions.explanation: The passage says that without steady prices many will continue with the more profitable crops.

questions.questionText: It can be inferred from the passage that the severe flooding in modern Bengaluru is largely due to
options: the loss of the linked system of lakes and channels
more rainfall than in earlier centuries
the vigilance of residents' groups
the cleaning of a few lakes by civic bodies
questions.explanation: The passage links floods to drained lakes and paved channels. It never claims rainfall has increased.

questions.questionText: The coaches mentioned in the passage would most probably agree that
options: children should combine online practice with games on a physical board
online platforms are useless for learning chess
teenagers should not play against grandmasters
tournament games should be shortened below six hours
questions.explanation: Their caution is that screens cannot teach temperament, which real boards do; they do not reject online play.

questions.questionText: The young man's remark about his cousin suggests that
options: many young people do not see handloom weaving as financially attractive
delivery riding is a respected traditional trade
government exhibitions have failed in every city
power looms are banned in the colony
questions.explanation: He contrasts weaving with the better earnings of a delivery rider, which points to weak financial appeal for youth.

questions.questionText: The author implies that the wellbeing measures taken by institutes
options: do not address the basic cause of student stress
have completely solved the problem
are unwelcome
are harmful to students
questions.explanation: 'Welcome, but they treat the symptoms' shows they help but do not reach the root cause.
